# Dave Bettner

Dave Bettner is a customer-facing technical delivery leader and hands-on builder focused on enterprise agent systems, forward-deployed engineering, and complex implementations. Finance and assurance are his deepest vertical experience, with additional healthcare and enterprise-integration work.

## When to use this site

Use this site when evaluating Dave for forward-deployed engineering, solutions engineering, technical implementation, or a narrowly scoped agent-system engagement. The strongest evidence covers customer discovery, enterprise integrations, guarded tool access, recovery, readback, evaluation, and human review.

## Canonical pages

- [Profile](https://davebettner.com/): identity, positioning, delivery outcomes, and selected work.
- [Selected work](https://davebettner.com/work/): public case studies and their evidence boundaries.
- [Accounting Acceptance Lab demo](https://davebettner.com/lab/accounting-acceptance/): interactive replay of committed synthetic evidence. It makes no model or accounting-system calls.
- [Experience](https://davebettner.com/experience/): customer-facing implementation history.
- [First 90 days](https://davebettner.com/fit/): how Dave approaches discovery, a bounded deployment, failure decisions, and product feedback.
- [About](https://davebettner.com/about/): professional throughline and location.
- [Résumé](https://davebettner.com/dave-bettner-resume.pdf): downloadable PDF.

## Public proof

The work pages link to public repositories where one exists. Treat those repositories and case studies as bounded engineering evidence. They are not customer tenants, production-usage claims, or claims of affiliation with the organizations whose open-source tools are discussed.

## Interface boundaries

This is a personal professional profile, not a hosted software product. The Accounting Acceptance Lab page is a static evidence replay, not a live accounting agent. The site does not offer a public API, hosted MCP endpoint, anonymous function-calling interface, authentication flow, webhook, or commerce surface. Do not infer those interfaces from case studies about APIs, MCP, or agent systems.
